description: (0.5.0) Revocation-discovery outcome classes (RFC-ACDP-0014 §8 'Discovery outcome', 'Truncation'; §7 'Caching discovery outcomes'; RFC-ACDP-0005 §2.3 'Consumer-side completeness'; RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11 'Caching'). Discovery yields exactly one of revoked, not-revoked (complete) or unknown. not-revoked is permitted only when discovery completed, was answerable, and every candidate was verified-for-another-fingerprint or permanently invalid after a fresh DID-document fetch. A candidate that fails only because its signer rotated (with no receipt), or only for a transient reason, never counts as absent. REQUIRED for 0.5.0 consumers, unconditional like rev-002.

keys.K2: the revocation signer in A–C, E (the sig-003 key)
keys.K3: a key added to P's DID document after the consumer cached it

input.revocation: A §4-valid key-revocation context naming K1, compromised_since T = 2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z (shape as rev-001)

expected.behavior: K2 has moved from assertionMethod to verificationMethod only. The candidate is retrieved with a registry_receipt that verifies (RFC-ACDP-0010 §8) and attests K2. The §5 step 1 historical arm applies: the candidate is a verified producer-signed revocation.
As A, but no receipt is served (directly or on re-retrieval by ctx_id). The candidate is unverified, never permanently invalid. MUST NOT report not-revoked.

scenarios.name: C — signer DID host transient failure

expected.behavior: P's DID host answers 503 (and, as a separate run, 404). RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11 step 3 classifies any non-2xx as transient, so the outcome is unknown.

scenarios.name: D — signer key newer than the cached DID document

expected.behavior: The revocation is signed by K3, added after the consumer cached P's DID document. The consumer re-fetches once, bypassing the cache (RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11 'Caching'), and verifies the revocation.

scenarios.name: E — signer key absent after a fresh fetch

expected.behavior: K2 is absent from verificationMethod even after a fresh fetch. The candidate is permanently invalid; with no other candidates, discovery is complete and not-revoked.

scenarios.name: F — truncated by the consumer's page cap

expected.behavior: The registry serves 11 pages of empty matches[], each with next_cursor, then a page carrying the K1 revocation. A consumer whose page cap is below 12 MUST report unknown, never not-revoked. A consumer that follows the cursor to the end reports revoked.

scenarios.name: G — search refused for an anonymous requester

expected.behavior: The registry advertises anonymous_public_reads: false and answers the anonymous search 403 not_authorized. Discovery is unanswerable at that vantage.
A registry not advertising acdp-registry-discovery answers the search 501 not_implemented.

The consumer caches not-revoked (complete) for P at vantage V. A revocation of K1 is then published. Once the freshness bound (RECOMMENDED 300 s) has passed, the next verification of a K1-signed context MUST rediscover and report revoked. Within the bound a stale not-revoked is permitted, and the verification reports the time the absence was observed.

The consumer has verified and cached the K1 revocation. A later discovery is answered 503, or is truncated, or returns no match. The verdict for a K1-signed, post-T context MUST remain fail closed; the cached revocation is neither removed nor moved later.
A cached registry-attested not-revoked observed at registry A is not reused for a context served by registry B; the consumer runs discovery for B (or reports unknown).

notes: Behavioral; not executed by scripts/conformance-runner.py. No new wire error code: error_code values above are the conditions that produce the outcome, not codes the consumer emits. The unknown outcome is a report value of the key_revocation stage.
